@servers.sheet.protocolSmb.sameAsSourceJustification: Apple keeps the protocol acronym verbatim in French macOS: NetAuthAgent `Localizable.loctable` key `SMB_PASSWORD` -> "Mot de passe SMB", NetworkSettingsIntents `Localizable.loctable` key `SMB` -> "SMB" (macOS 26.6.2 build 25G83, 2026-09-06). It is also on the catalog's own brand list.

@servers.sheet.protocolSftp.sameAsSourceJustification: Apple keeps the protocol acronym verbatim in French macOS: Sharing.appex `Localizable.loctable` key `SSH_INFO_GENERAL` -> "La connexion à distance autorise les utilisateurs d'autres ordinateurs à accéder à cet ordinateur via SSH et SFTP." (macOS 26.6.2 build 25G83, 2026-09-06).

@servers.sheet.protocolWebdav.sameAsSourceJustification: Apple keeps the protocol name verbatim in French macOS: NetAuthAgent `Localizable.loctable` key `WEBDAV_PASSWORD` -> "Mot de passe WebDAV", WorkflowKit `Localizable.loctable` -> "serveurs SMB/CIFS, NFS, FTP (lecture seule) ou WebDAV" (macOS 26.6.2 build 25G83, 2026-09-06). The shipped `servers.refusal.notAWebdavServer` already keeps it.

@servers.sheet.addressPlaceholder.sameAsSourceJustification: A literal example hostname, not prose: `nas` is the same abbreviation in French (the shipped `servers.hub.emptyMessage` writes "un Mac ou un NAS") and `.local` is the reserved mDNS suffix macOS itself shows (Finder `ConnectToWindow.strings` fr placeholder "Adresse du serveur" takes the same form). Translating it would print an address that does not resolve.

@servers.sheet.protocolS3.sameAsSourceJustification: A protocol name, kept verbatim like the sibling SMB, SFTP, and WebDAV options (Apple keeps protocol acronyms in French macOS, see `servers.sheet.protocolWebdav`); the AWS French docs also write "Amazon S3" and "compatible S3" unchanged (docs.aws.amazon.com/fr_fr, 2026-10-02).

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderAws.sameAsSourceJustification: "Amazon S3" is a product name its vendor ships unchanged in French (the @key says to keep it as-is), like the neighboring provider choices; translating it would name a product that doesn't exist. AWS French documentation writes "Amazon S3" (docs.aws.amazon.com/fr_fr, 2026-10-02).

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderR2.sameAsSourceJustification: "Cloudflare R2" is a product name its vendor ships unchanged in French (the @key says to keep it as-is), like the neighboring provider choices; translating it would name a product that doesn't exist.

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderB2.sameAsSourceJustification: "Backblaze B2" is a product name its vendor ships unchanged in French (the @key says to keep it as-is), like the neighboring provider choices; translating it would name a product that doesn't exist.

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderWasabi.sameAsSourceJustification: "Wasabi" is a product name its vendor ships unchanged in French (the @key says to keep it as-is), like the neighboring provider choices; translating it would name a product that doesn't exist.

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderHetzner.sameAsSourceJustification: "Hetzner Object Storage" is a product name its vendor ships unchanged in French (the @key says to keep it as-is), like the neighboring provider choices; translating it would name a product that doesn't exist. Hetzner publishes no French UI, so the English product name is the only one a French user sees.

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderGcs.sameAsSourceJustification: "Google Cloud Storage" is a product name its vendor ships unchanged in French (the @key says to keep it as-is), like the neighboring provider choices; translating it would name a product that doesn't exist. Google’s French console keeps "Cloud Storage" as the product name.

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderDigitalOcean.sameAsSourceJustification: "DigitalOcean Spaces" is a product name its vendor ships unchanged in French (the @key says to keep it as-is), like the neighboring provider choices; translating it would name a product that doesn't exist. DigitalOcean publishes no French UI.

@servers.paneState.retryTotalMinutes.sameAsSourceJustification: French spells the unit exactly like English, singular and plural alike: « 1 minute », « 2 minutes ». The value IS translated (it carries French's own one/many/other categories, and the sibling seconds key reads « seconde »/« secondes »); there is simply no other French word for a minute.
